key_insight: Accelerating verifiable AI requires matching hardware and proof-system optimizations to workload-specific bottlenecks, rather than optimizing cryptographic kernels in isolation.
engineering_relevance: Engineers must assess memory capacity, instruction issue and synchronization alongside execution time and bandwidth when selecting hardware for zero-knowledge proving.
method: Link AI workloads, proof systems, cryptographic kernels and hardware through a four-layer framework.
Review the literature and measure six provers and seven kernels.
Analyze bottlenecks to guide hardware selection and proof-system optimization.
evidence_signal: Measurements show shifting costs across proof systems and input lengths; a 13-billion-parameter fine-tuning configuration exceeds 40 GB GPU capacity but completes on an 80 GB device.
watch_item: Kernel-level speedups may not translate into end-to-end gains when memory capacity or other proof-generation stages dominate.
paper_title: Infrastructure for Verifiable AI: Where Proof Costs Go and How Hardware Can Help
